Information since May points to a strong labor market and moderate growth, but with soft business fixed investment and inflation running below 2 percent while market-based inflation compensation has declined. In policy-rule terms (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Taylor-rule frameworks), downside inflation and rising uncertainty (Baker, Bloom, and Davis on economic policy uncertainty) justify a cautious, dovish bias and “risk-management” posture—consistent with the FOMC’s “act as appropriate” language and the use of IOER/ON RRP to implement the target range (Goodfriend, 2002). That said, term-structure research (Ang and Piazzesi; Rudebusch and Wu) warns that lower inflation compensation can partly reflect changing risk premia, tempering how negative the signal is. Bullard’s dissent for a 25 bp cut underscores this dovish tilt. Net tone: cautious/dovish but not alarmist.
